episodes.194262: A shortwave trough moved south from Colorado over New Mexico on September 5th. This combined with upslope surface flow from a backdoor front resulted in the development of showers and storms over the northern mountains moving south and east across lower elevations during the afternoon and evening hours. These showers and storms resulted in some flash flooding over the HPCC burn scar and at Bandelier National Monument along with some large hail and severe thunderstorm wind gusts north of Albuquerque, the East Mountain Communities, and across the White Sands Missile Range. Strong east canyon wind gusts were observed across the Albuquerque Metro and across the White Sands Missile Range in the south central highlands during the evening hours as storm outflow combined with the backdoor front moved through. Showers and storms gradually dissipated across south central New Mexico after sunset.
episodes.195833: A waterspout developed off of the coast of the Patrick Space Force Base.
episodes.196151: Another wet, unsettled day continued across much of NE FL and coastal SE GA as a surface front draped across north FL lifted slowly northward. Locally, near record high |deep layer moisture with PWAT values 2-2.5 inches were in place with weak steering flow. Waves of morning coastal rainfall expanded inland with diurnal heating.
episodes.196661: Unsettled weather conditions prevailed across Puerto Rico through the first week of September as a retrograding upper level trough lingered in the region. The instability of the trough, diurnal heating, and low level moisture combined to generate widespread showers and thunderstorms across the region. Each day, accumulations ranged from 2 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts up to 5 inches in some areas. This led to several reports of mudslides, lightning, and gusty winds.
episodes.196981: A stalled boundary along the LA coast in association with a stationary low in the northeast Gulf created multiple rounds of heavy rain. This caused some isolated flash flooding along the I-12 corridor in Baton Rouge and St. Tammany Parish.
episodes.197100: A landspout developed west of Kingfisher on the afternoon of the 5th.

At 8 PM EDT, broadcast media shared a video showing Main St near 8th St was flooded. Floodwaters reached halfway up tires. About 3 to 4 inches of rain fell by this time. At 8:32 pm, emergency management reported that Jefferson Street and the UF Health parking lot was flooded. This is a known flood-prone site due to its proximity to Hogans Creek. About 3 to 4.5 inches of rain had fallen in this area. Videos were later shared showing floodwaters reached up to a woman's waist and above tires on an SUV. Floodwaters began entering homes along Moncrief Creek including along Leonard Cir E and Moncrief Rd. Floodwaters were deep enough that JFRD was unable to evacuate residents from a home along Leonard Cir E. Old St. Augustine Rd and Pritmore Rd were closed due to flooding. Widespread flooding with numerous cars stuck in floodwaters were reported across the San Marco, Downtown Jacksonville, Riverside, Ortega, Avondale, Hogan's Creek, Moncrief park, and Norwood areas.
